examples: The tiger looks fierce.
A fierce dog barked at us.
The storm was fierce.

more.def: Wild, strong, and ready to attack; or very strong and powerful.
examples: A fierce wind bent the trees almost to the ground.
The fierce lion roared to protect her cubs.
The two teams were in a fierce battle for first place.
They had a fight.
The fight was about a toy.
We made up after the fight.

more.def: An angry argument or struggle between people or groups.
examples: The brothers had a fight about whose turn it was.
They made up after their fight and shook hands.
A fight between the two dogs ended when I called them.

easy.def: To work hard against something bad.
examples: Firefighters fight fires.
Doctors fight sickness.
We fight to win.

more.def: To try hard to stop or defeat something bad.
examples: Firefighters fought the blaze all through the night.
Doctors work hard to fight disease.
The village worked together to fight the flood.
The figure is ten.
Draw a figure.
I see a figure.

more.def: A number or amount, or the shape of a person or object.
examples: The figure on the chart showed that sales had grown.
A tall figure stood at the end of the hall.
The artist drew a figure of a dancer.
I figure it out.
Can you figure it out?
She figured out the puzzle.

more.def: To work out the answer by thinking.
examples: I figured out the riddle after thinking for a while.
Can you figure out how much money we need?
He figured that the bus would be late.

easy.def: To see or get something that was lost.
examples: I find my shoe.
She found a coin.
Can you find the cat?

more.def: To discover something, or to get something back that was lost.
examples: We found a bird's nest in the tall grass.
I could not find my glasses anywhere in the house.
The explorers found a hidden cave behind the waterfall.
I feel fine.
The weather is fine.
That is a fine idea.

more.def: Very good, or healthy and well enough.
examples: It was a fine day for a picnic by the lake.
I fell off my bike, but I am fine.
The artist did a fine job on the painting.
The thread is fine.
She has fine hair.
The sand is fine.
The spider spun a fine web between the two branches.
The beach had fine white sand that felt soft under our feet.
He drew the lines with a fine pen.

easy.def: To come to the end of something.
examples: I finish my homework first.
She finished her lunch.
Let me finish my story.

more.def: To reach the end of something you were doing, so that nothing is left to do.
examples: Please finish your breakfast before you get dressed.
The runners finished the race in under ten minutes.
He finished painting the fence just before the rain came.

easy.def: The end of a race or a story.
examples: It was a close finish.
The book has a happy finish.
The runners raced to the finish.

more.def: The end part of something, such as a race or a story.
examples: The two swimmers touched the wall together at a very close finish.
The movie had an exciting finish that made everyone cheer.
The cyclists sprinted toward the finish.

easy.def: Flames that give heat and light.
examples: The fire is hot.
We sat by the fire.
Fire needs air.

more.def: The heat, light, and flames made when something burns.
examples: We roasted marshmallows over the campfire.
The firefighters put out the fire at the old barn.
Fire needs air to keep burning.
I was the first in line.
This is my first day.
She won first prize.

more.def: Coming before all others in time, order, or importance.
examples: The first snow of the year fell last night.
Read the first chapter before the next class.
Who was the first person to fly an airplane?
Wash your hands first.
I will go first.
First, mix the eggs.

more.def: Before anything else, or at the very start.
examples: First, crack the eggs into a bowl.
She arrived first and saved us all a seat.
We first met when I was six.
I have five fingers.
Five plus one is six.
She is five years old.

more.def: The number 5, which is one more than four.
examples: A starfish usually has five arms.
We counted five ducks on the pond.
The bell rings at five minutes to three.
Dad will fix my bike.
She fixed the toy.
Can you fix this?

more.def: To repair something that is broken or not working.
examples: Dad fixed the leak under the sink.
She fixed the tear in her jacket.
The mechanic fixes cars at the shop.

easy.def: To make food or a drink.
examples: Mom fixes lunch.
I will fix a snack.
Dad fixed dinner.

more.def: To prepare food or a drink.
examples: Dad fixed pancakes for breakfast.
Can I fix you a cup of tea?
She fixed sandwiches for the picnic.
